_notes: IMPORT PATH — READ THIS BEFORE EDITING. This hook does a MODULE-TOP-LEVEL import of the
shared parser: sys.path.insert(<hook dir>/../scripts/workshop) then
`from workshop_slide_table import build_index`. The parity harness extracts only hooks/*.py
into a temp dir, so that relative path does not exist there and EVERY case would die with
ModuleNotFoundError (exit 1, empty stdout) — pinning nothing at all, and letting a TS port
that merely crashes pass. Every case therefore sets PYTHONPATH to the LIVE repo's
scripts/workshop + scripts/lib so the Python side loads the same parser the TS port will
mirror. PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 keeps CPython from dropping __pycache__/ into the fixture
dir, which would otherwise show up as a Python-only filesystem delta.
If the repo is checked out elsewhere, PYTHONPATH here must be updated — a stale path fails
LOUDLY (py exits 1, ts does not), it never silently passes.
The hook itself is pure: no files written, no subprocesses. Every case's expected fs delta
is empty.
Branch map (all 9 outcome branches of the source are covered and were verified by running
the HEAD .py against these exact fixtures):
argv form  -> violations (exit 1 report) | stale_approval (WARN, exit 0) | clean (exit 0)
stdin form -> unreadable stdin (silent 0) | non-Write/Edit tool (silent 0) |
file_path not *OUTLINE_APPROVED.md (silent 0) | violations (deny JSON) |
stale_approval (allow JSON + warning) | clean (silent 0)
deny-outline-md-missing pins a real quirk worth locking down: fp.parent/'OUTLINE.md' is fed
to build_index(), which — because that path is not an existing file — treats it as a
DIRECTORY and reports 'OUTLINE.md not found at .planning/OUTLINE.md/OUTLINE.md'. The doubled
segment is the actual HEAD behavior; the port must reproduce it byte for byte.
